title: Adversarial data-free minimax framework for combined distillation, quantization and pruning
content:
A unified data-free training framework jointly trains a compact student network with quantization or pruning constraints and an auxiliary generator in a minimax (adversarial) formulation. The framework optimizes the minimax objective
      $$
      \min_{\theta_s}\max_{\theta_g}\ \mathbb{E}_{z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I)}\; \mathcal{D}\big(z;\theta_g,\theta_s\big),
      $$
      where the divergence term is defined as
      $$
      \mathcal{D}(z;\theta_g,\theta_s)=D\big(T(G(z;\theta_g))\,\|\,S(G(z;\theta_g);\theta_s)\big),
      $$
      with $T(x;\theta_0)$ a fixed pre-trained teacher network, $S(x;\theta_s)$ the compact student network, $G(z;\theta_g)$ the auxiliary generator taking input $z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I)$, and $D(\cdot\|\cdot)$ a probability divergence between teacher and student outputs (e.g., Kullback-Leibler divergence $D_{KL}$ or symmetric Jensen–Shannon divergence $D_{JS}$). The full training loss includes a spatial-attention regularizer
      $$
      \mathcal{R}_a(z;\theta_s)=\beta\sum_{l\in\mathcal{S}_a}\Big\|\frac{f(s_l)}{\|f(s_l)\|}-\frac{f(t_l)}{\|f(t_l)\|}\Big\|,
      $$
      with $f(x)=\frac{1}{N_c}\sum_c (x^{(c)})^2$ the per-layer spatial attention map averaged over channels, and a pruning sparsity regularizer
      $$
      \mathcal{R}_p(\theta_s)=\sum_{l=1}^L \gamma_l\|s_l\|_1 + \lambda\|W_l\|_F^2 + \lambda\|b_l\|^2,
      $$
      where $s_l\in\mathbb{R}^{n_l}$ are trainable per-filter scaling factors for layer $l$ and $W_l,b_l$ are the layer weights and biases. Quantization is implemented via a BinaryConnect-like scheme: (a) a full-precision buffer $\theta_b$ is maintained, (b) the gradient is computed from the binary weights $\delta\operatorname{sign}(\theta_b)$, (c) the buffer is updated via gradient descent and then projected onto the infinity-norm ball of radius $\delta$ (clipped to $[-\delta,\delta]$). After training, the binary weights are set to $\delta\operatorname{sign}(\theta_b)$. This formulation integrates knowledge distillation, adversarial synthetic-data generation, BinaryConnect quantization, and structured pruning with $\ell_1$ penalties on per-filter scaling factors into a single practical training procedure.

title: Data-free binary quantization achieves high CIFAR-10 accuracy
content: Using the adversarial data-free minimax framework with BinaryConnect-style quantization (binary weights in intermediate layers, full-precision first and final layers, and a fixed per-layer scale factor $\delta$), a binary-weight student Wide ResNet WRN-16-2 distilled from a WRN-40-2 teacher on the CIFAR-10 dataset attains a test accuracy of 88.14% in the data-free setting. Initializing the binary student weights as $\theta_s(0)=\delta\operatorname{sign}(\theta_0)$ where $\theta_0$ are pretrained weights improves the data-free binary accuracy to 88.98%. For reference, a full-precision WRN-16-2 trained in the same data-free setting achieves 89.71%, and a WRN-16-2 trained with supervised BinaryConnect and data augmentation reaches 92.97%. These empirical numbers demonstrate that extreme low-bit (binary) quantization of intermediate layers can be achieved without access to training data while preserving most of the full-precision data-free performance.

title: Data-free structured pruning achieves strong compression–accuracy tradeoffs
content: Applying the adversarial data-free minimax framework with per-filter scaling factors $s_l$ and $\ell_1$ sparsity penalties $\gamma_l$ plus weight decay $\lambda$ to a WRN-16-2 network on CIFAR-10 yields substantial parameter and floating-point operation (FLOP) reductions while retaining high test accuracy. Varying $\lambda$ from $1\times10^{-5}$ to $6\times10^{-5}$ (with $\gamma=2\times10^{-3}$ and pruning threshold $t_s=0.1$) reduces the number of parameters from $570,000$ to $323,000$ and test accuracy from $92.77\%$ to $89.17\%$. With grid-searched pruning hyperparameters, a data-free pruned WRN-16-2 with approximately $339,000$ parameters and $52.3\text{ million}$ FLOPs achieves $90.57\%$ accuracy; a "Data-free + Warm up" schedule yields $254,000$ parameters and $48.2\text{ million}$ FLOPs with $89.19\%$ accuracy. Increasing weight decay by a factor of 6 leads to roughly a $43\%$ reduction in parameter count in the examined setting. The generator's synthesized images become visually sharper as $\lambda$ increases, correlating with higher compression ratios.

title: Convergence guarantee for data-free quantization with O(1/√k) duality-gap bound
content:
For the quantized minimax optimization with variables $x$ (quantized student parameters) and $y$ (generator parameters), consider the stochastic alternating update scheme
      $$
      \begin{aligned}
      \hat{x}_{k+1} &= \hat{x}_k - \alpha_k g_x(x_k,y_k),\\
      x_{k+1} &= \mathcal{Q}(\hat{x}_{k+1}),\\
      y_{k+1} &= y_k + \beta_k g_y(x_{k+1},y_k),
      \end{aligned}
      $$
      where $\mathbb{E}[g_x]=\nabla_x\mathcal{F}$, $\mathbb{E}[g_y]=\nabla_y\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{Q}(x)=\delta\operatorname{sign}(x)$ is the quantization operator, and $P(x,y)=\mathcal{F}(x,y^\star)-\mathcal{F}(x^\star,y)$ is the primal–dual gap relative to an assumed saddle $(x^\star,y^\star)$. If $\mathcal{F}$ is convex in $x$, concave in $y$, Lipschitz in function values (constant $L$), has Lipschitz partial gradients (constants $L_x$, $L_y$), and stochastic gradients have bounded second moments (bounds $G_x^2$, $G_y^2$), and if the distances to the optimal solution are bounded ($\mathbb{E}\|x_k-x^\star\|^2\leq D_x^2$, $\mathbb{E}\|y_k-y^\star\|^2\leq D_y^2$), then choosing step sizes $\alpha_k=C_\alpha/\sqrt{k}$ and $\beta_k=C_\beta/\sqrt{k}$ yields the expected duality-gap bound
      $$
      \begin{aligned}
      \mathbb{E}\big[P(\bar{x}^l,\bar{y}^l)\big] \le&\; \frac{1}{2\sqrt{l}}\Big(\frac{D_x^2}{C_\alpha}+\frac{D_y^2}{C_\beta}\Big) \\
      &+\frac{\sqrt{l+1}}{2l}\Big(C_\alpha G_x^2 + C_\alpha L_y G_x^2 + C_\alpha L_y D_y^2 + C_\beta G_y^2\Big) \\
      &+ (L_x D_x + L D_x + 2 L_y D_y)\sqrt{d}\,\Delta,
      \end{aligned}
      $$
      where $\bar{x}^l=\frac{1}{l}\sum_{k=1}^l x^k$, $\bar{y}^l=\frac{1}{l}\sum_{k=1}^l y^k$, $d$ is the parameter dimension, $\Delta$ is the quantization grain (so $\|\mathcal{Q}(x)-x\|\le\sqrt{d}\Delta$), and $L, L_x, L_y, G_x, G_y, D_x, D_y$ are the Lipschitz, gradient-variance, and distance constants defined in the assumptions. The bound implies an $O(1/\sqrt{k})$ convergence rate of the expected duality gap down to a neighborhood determined by the quantization resolution $\Delta$.

title: Linear convergence to stationary points for data-free pruning under two-sided PL condition
content:
For the pruning minimax problem with full (deterministic) gradient access, let $\mathcal{F}(x,y)$ be $L$-smooth, possess at least one stationary point, and satisfy the two-sided Polyak–Łojasiewicz (PL) condition: there exist $\mu_1,\mu_2>0$ such that
      $$
      \tfrac{1}{2}\|\nabla_x\mathcal{F}(x,y)\|^2 \ge \mu_1\big[\mathcal{F}(x,y)-\min_x\mathcal{F}(x,y)\big],\quad
      \tfrac{1}{2}\|\nabla_y\mathcal{F}(x,y)\|^2 \ge \mu_2\big[\max_y\mathcal{F}(x,y)-\mathcal{F}(x,y)\big].
      $$
      With alternating gradient updates
      $$
      x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_k\nabla_x\mathcal{F}(x_k,y_k),\qquad
      y_{k+1}=y_k+\beta_k\nabla_y\mathcal{F}(x_{k+1},y_k),
      $$
      and constant step sizes $\alpha=\frac{\mu_2^2}{18L^3}$, $\beta=1/L$, the potential
      $$
      P_k := a_k + \lambda b_k,\quad a_k=h(x_k)-h^\star,\ b_k=h(x_k)-\mathcal{F}(x_k,y_k),\ h(x)=\max_y\mathcal{F}(x,y),\ h^\star=\min_x h(x),
      $$
      contracts linearly for a suitable constant $\lambda$:
      $$
      P_k \le \Big(1-\frac{\mu_1\mu_2^2}{36L^3}\Big)^k P_0.
      $$
      Consequently, the stationary residual $\|\nabla_x\mathcal{F}(x_k,y_k)\|^2+\|\nabla_y\mathcal{F}(x_k,y_k)\|^2$ decays at the same exponential rate up to problem-dependent constants.

title: Symmetric Jensen–Shannon divergence improves pruning stability and pseudo-data quality
content: Empirically for pruning, using the symmetric Jensen–Shannon divergence $D_{JS}(x\|y)=\tfrac{1}{2}D_{KL}(x\|y)+\tfrac{1}{2}D_{KL}(y\|x)$ as the distillation/divergence loss for the adversarial generator yields improved stability and better compression results compared with using $D_{KL}$ alone. Under comparable hyperparameter settings, the average teacher entropy on generated batches is lower with JSD (e.g., entropy $0.87$) than with KLD (e.g., entropy $0.93$), and JSD configurations produce equal-or-higher compression ratios and more stable accuracies (KLD sometimes collapsed to $73.48\%$ accuracy when $\gamma$ increased while JSD maintained accuracy).

organized_parts.label: assertion
organized_parts.content: Empirically for pruning, using the symmetric Jensen–Shannon divergence as the distillation/divergence loss for the adversarial generator yields improved stability and better compression results compared with using $D_{KL}$ alone.

title: Winning lottery tickets from supervised training transfer to data-free training
content: Subnetworks ("winning tickets") discovered by iterative magnitude pruning in a supervised setting, when trained under the data-free adversarial minimax framework with their original initializations, achieve higher CIFAR-10 test accuracies than the same pruned structures initialized randomly. For a WRN-16-2 pruned to 53.0K parameters, the ticket initialization attains 77.03% test accuracy under data-free training versus 75.48% for a random initialization; for a 45.5K-parameter ticket, the ticket initialization yields 74.66% versus 73.56% for random initialization. These results indicate that the inductive bias encapsulated by winning-ticket initializations improves generalization even when the training procedure is data-free and the optimizer and hyperparameters differ from the supervised discovery process.

title: Spatial-attention regularization stabilizes data-free distillation for quantization and pruning
content:
Incorporating spatial-attention matching regularization between student and teacher feature maps,
      $$
      \mathcal{R}_a(z;\theta_s)=\beta\sum_{l\in\mathcal{S}_a}\Big\|\frac{f(s_l)}{\|f(s_l)\|}-\frac{f(t_l)}{\|f(t_l)\|}\Big\|,
      $$
      where $\mathcal{S}_a$ is a selected subset of layers (e.g., layers before spatial down-sampling), $\beta$ is a scaling coefficient, $s_l$ and $t_l$ are the feature maps of the student and teacher networks at layer $l$, and $f(x)=\frac{1}{N_c}\sum_c (x^{(c)})^2$ computes the spatial attention map as the mean of squared features over channels, empirically improves stability and performance of the adversarial data-free training for both quantization and pruning. Including this attention regularizer alongside the adversarial divergence and sparsity penalties leads to more stable student training in the experiments.
